To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified 30 genetic variants in 17 regions of the genome that are associated with blood pressure, and that these variants explain about 1.2% of the variation in blood pressure.
we identified 16 novel genetic loci associated with systolic or diastolic blood pressures, which provide new clues into the biology and genetics of high blood pressure.
We performed a genome wide association study (GWAS) of systolic and of diastolic blood pressures, in over 200,000 participants, and identified 29 loci associated with blood pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of hypertension and related traits.
the genetic basis of human disease, with a particular focus on cardiovascular disease.
the genetics of blood pressure and related phenotypes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the genetic architecture of blood pressure is highly complex, involving multiple genes of small effect, and that these genes are involved in many biological pathways, some of which are known to regulate blood pressure and some of which are novel.
this study provides new insights into the genetic basis of blood pressure, hypertension and cardiovascular disease.
genetic variants in novel pathways influence blood pressure and cardiovascular disease risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we identified 16 new loci for blood pressure, and that these loci were associated with blood pressure and with hypertension in populations of European descent, as well as in populations of East Asian, South-Asian and African ancestry.
we have identified 29 genetic variants that influence blood pressure and that collectively these variants explain 1.2% of the variance of blood pressure in the population.
the genetic architecture of blood pressure is more complex than we previously thought.

blood pressure is heritable.
there is a lot of genetic overlap between the risk factors for cardiovascular disease, including high blood pressure.
blood pressure is a herit able trait influenced by many different genes.
